newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin op preparation to take 6-8 weeks - doctors.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin op preparation to take 6-8 weeks - doctors.

text.p: It will take 6-8 weeks to prepare Boris Yeltsin for an operation on his heart, but the surgery should enable the Russian president to work normally, doctors advising the president said on Wednesday.

"After reviewing all facts I am pleased to say that the operation is needed, that it shall provide excellent results," pioneering U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey told a news briefing. "After the operation the president will soon be restored to normal."
The doctors said Yeltsin was likely to stay in hospital until the operation.

DeBakey, who pioneered heart bypass operations, had joined a team of specialists examining the president on Wednesday and deciding when to operate. Yeltsin, 65, has been in hospital since September 13. He had two heart attacks last year.

Russian surgeon Andrei Vorobyov, the head of the council of doctors, said Yeltsin's heavy workload during the summer had "caused complications which make the operation undesirable today". He expected Yeltsin to work in hospital while doctors prepared him for the operation.

Renat Akchurin, who is expected to lead the operating team, said he shared DeBakey's optimism about the surgery, which will improve the blood supply to Yeltsin's heart. But he added: "We will need 6-8 weeks to minimise the risk of the operation."
